newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SE Asian Cocoa - Prices steady, buck New York's fall.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian Cocoa - Prices steady, buck New York's fall.

text.p: Southeast Asian cocoa prices held steady on Wednesday, bucking the sharp fall of cocoa futures prices in New York, and traders said projected demand should keep sentiment strong.

Prices in Malaysia took a slight dip but were supported by projections of purchases in the near future by consumers, dealers said. They were also firm in Indonesia on assurances by local dealers that business would remain stable.
New York cocoa futures tumbled to eight week lows on Tuesday on heavy speculative long liquidation with the July contract finishing US$40 down on the day at $1,414 a tonne.
"The price held because of guarantees given by traders to growers in an effort to keep their loyalty in a very competitive market," a trader in Indonesia said.
Traders in Kuala Lumpur said demand for beans was still steady although most grinders and confectioners had enough for immediate use.
"It's an ongoing buying exercise and I think the market price is reflective of this," a trader in Malaysia said.
Crop arrivals in both countries were already strong and expectations of a good harvest were high.
"When the price goes up, the price goes up, but when it goes down it adjusts very slowly," a dealer in Indonesia said.
Indonesian cocoa out of the main growing district of Ujung Pandang was quoted at 2,950-2,975 rupiah/kg on Wednesday.

The Malaysian Cocoa Board quoted Standard Malaysian Cocoa (SMC) Grade 1 A out of Tawau, the country's main growing area, at an average of 3,350 ringgit a tonne, down 25 ringgit from the previous week.

The board quoted the SMC 1B grade out of Tawau at an average of 3,300 ringgit, also down 75 ringgit from last week. Traders offered the SMC 1A at 3,300 ringgit a tonne and the SMC IB at 3,375-3,385 ringgit.
(With a contribution from Jim Della-Giacomo in Jakarta)
